Let \(E,F\) be Banach spaces and \(C\geqslant 1\). We write \(E\simeq_{C}F\) if there exists an isomorphism \(T\colon E\to F\) with \(\lVert T\rVert\,\lVert T^{-1}\rVert\leqslant C\). We set

\(d_{BM}(E,F)=\inf\{\lVert T\rVert\,\|T^{-1}\|:\ T\colon E\to F\text{ is an isomorphism}\}.\)

Thus \(d_{BM}(E,F)\leq C\) if and only if, for every ε > 0, there is an isomorphism of distortion at most C + ε.

Correction in this reading edition

The printed equivalence at the endpoint need not follow from an infimum. The approximate bound displayed here is the equivalence proved in Lean.

Let \(C\colon[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)\) be an increasing function. A Banach space \(E\) is \(C\)-primary if for every bounded projection \(P\colon E\to E\) one has

\(PE\simeq_{C(\max\{1,\lVert P\rVert\})}E\qquad\text{or}\qquad(\mathrm{Id}_{E}-P)E\simeq_{C(\max\{1,\lVert P\rVert\})}E.\)

We call \(E\) uniformly primary if it is \(C\)-primary for some such function \(C\).

Correction in this reading edition

The control function is defined on [1, ∞). Evaluating it at max(1, ‖P‖) includes the zero projection; this is the thesis convention.

results.title: (Pełczyński decomposition method ).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be Banach spaces such that \(X\) is isomorphic to a complemented subspace of \(Y\) and \(Y\) is isomorphic to a complemented subspace of \(X\). Suppose further that

  1. (a)

    \(X\simeq X\oplus X\) and \(Y\simeq Y\oplus Y\), or

  2. (b)

    \(X\simeq c_{0}(X)\) or \(X\simeq\ell_{p}(X)\) for some \(1\leqslant p\leqslant\infty\).

Then \(X\simeq Y\).

Let \(E\) be a Banach space.

  1. (a)

    We say that \(E\) has the primary factorisation property (PFP) if for every bounded operator \(T\colon E\to E\), the identity \(\mathrm{Id}_{E}\) factors either through \(T\) or through \(\mathrm{Id}_{E}-T\).

  2. (b)

    Let \(C\geqslant 1\). We say that \(E\) has the \(C\)-primary factorisation property (\(C\)-PFP) if for every bounded operator \(T\colon E\to E\) there exist bounded operators \(U,V\colon E\to E\) such that either

    \(UTV=\mathrm{Id}_{E}\quad\text{ or }\quad U(\mathrm{Id}_{E}-T)V=\mathrm{Id}_{E}\)

    and \(\lVert U\rVert\,\lVert V\rVert\leqslant C.\)

  3. (c)

    Let \(C\geqslant 1\). We say that \(E\) has the \(C^{+}\)-primary factorisation property (\(C^{+}\)-PFP) if it has the \((C+\varepsilon)\)-PFP for every \(\varepsilon>0\).

  4. (d)

    We say that \(E\) has the uniform primary factorisation property (UPFP) if there exists \(C\geqslant 1\) such that \(E\) has the \(C\)-PFP.
Let \(E,F\) be Banach spaces and let \(S\colon E\to F\) be an isomorphism. If \(F\) has the \(C\)-PFP, then \(E\) has the \(C\,\lVert S\rVert^{2}\lVert S^{-1}\rVert^{2}\)-PFP.

Assume that E is nonzero.

Let \(E\) be a Banach space and set

\(\mathcal{M}_{E}=\{T\in\mathcal{B}(E):\ \mathrm{Id}_{E}\text{ does not factor through }T\}.\)

Then \(E\) has the PFP if and only if \(\mathcal{M}_{E}\) is a maximal ideal of \(\mathcal{B}(E)\). In this case \(\mathcal{M}_{E}\) is the unique maximal ideal of \(\mathcal{B}(E)\).

Correction in this reading edition

The nonzero hypothesis is necessary. For the zero space the set of nonfactorising operators is empty, so the printed equivalence fails.

The preceding proposition identifies the PFP with the assertion that the specific set \(\mathcal{M}_{E}\) is a maximal ideal. It should not be read as saying that the mere existence of a unique maximal ideal in \(\mathcal{B}(E)\) automatically implies the PFP: in examples where a unique maximal ideal is known by other means, one must still verify that it coincides with \(\mathcal{M}_{E}\).

Let \((e_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) be a normalised unconditional basis of a Banach space \(X\). Then no subsequence of \((e_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) spans a subspace isomorphic to \(\ell_{1}\) if and only if \(\lim_{m\to\infty}e_{n}^{*}(Te_{m})=0\) for any operator \(T\colon X\to X\) and any \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a normalised \(1\)-unconditional basis \((e_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\), and let \(T\colon X\to X\) be bounded. Suppose there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that

\(|e_{m}^{*}Te_{n}|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{n+m}}\qquad(m,n\in\mathbb{N}).\)

Then \(\lVert T\rVert\leqslant\varepsilon\).
Let \(X\) be a separable Banach space with a symmetric basis, not equivalent to the \(\ell_{1}\)-basis, and a symmetric norm. Then \(X\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.

The same argument applies to spaces with a subsymmetric basis after replacing the isometric subsequence identifications by the canonical isomorphisms supplied by subsymmetry and tracking the corresponding constants. The non-separable setting is treated separately in Section 4.

Let \(Y=X_{1}(X_{2}(\dots(X_{N-1}(X_{N}))))\) and \(T\colon Y\to Y\) be an operator. We define the property of a sequence \(J\in\bigcup_{k=1}^{N}\mathbb{N}^{k}\) supporting \(T\) by backward induction on the length of \(J\):

  1. (1)

    Base Case (\(|J|=N\)): A sequence \(I\in\mathbb{N}^{N}\) supports \(T\) if \(|e_{I}^{*}Te_{I}|\geqslant 1/2\).

  2. (2)

    Inductive Step (\(|J|<N)\): A sequence \(J\in\mathbb{N}^{k}\) (for \(1\leqslant k<N\)) supports \(T\) if the set of extensions

    \(\{j\in\mathbb{N}:J\smallfrown(j)\text{ supports }T\}\)

    is infinite.

Let \(Y=X_{1}(X_{2}(\cdots(X_{N-1}(X_{N}))))\) and let \(T\in\mathcal{B}(Y)\). Then one of the two operators \(T\) and \(\mathrm{Id}_{Y}-T\) is supported by infinitely many first-level nodes \((i_{1})\).

results.title: (CKL tree selection).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(Y=X_{1}(X_{2}(\cdots(X_{N-1}(X_{N}))))\), where each \(X_{j}\) has a symmetric basis not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\). Let \(T\in\mathcal{B}(Y)\) and let \(\eta>0\). Suppose that infinitely many first-level nodes support \(T\). Then there is a subset \(\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathbb{N}^{N}\), order-isomorphic to \(\mathbb{N}^{N}\) in the natural tree sense, such that

\(Z=[e_{I}:I\in\mathcal{A}]\)

is isometrically isomorphic to \(Y\), every \(I\in\mathcal{A}\) satisfies

\(|e_{I}^{*}Te_{I}|\geqslant\tfrac{1}{2},\)

and, after enumerating \(\mathcal{A}\) as \((I_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\),

\(|e_{I_{j}}^{*}Te_{I_{k}}|<\frac{\eta}{2^{j+k+1}}\qquad(j\neq k).\)

Let \(X_{1},\dots,X_{N}\) be Banach spaces with symmetric norms and symmetric bases \(\mathcal{E}_{j}\), none of which is equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\). Then the Banach space \(Y=X_{1}(X_{2}(\dots(X_{N-1}(X_{N}))))\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.

Let \(T\colon\ell_{1}\to\ell_{1}\) be an operator. Then for any \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists an infinite subset \(M=\{m_{k}:k\in\mathbb{N}\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that for all \(k<j\) we have \(|e_{m_{k}}^{*}Te_{m_{j}}|<\varepsilon.\)

Let \(T\colon\ell_{1}\to\ell_{1}\) be an operator. Suppose that there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that for all \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) we have

\(\sum_{m\in\mathbb{N}}|e^{*}_{m}Te_{n}|<\varepsilon.\)

Then \(\lVert T\rVert\leqslant\varepsilon\).
The space \(\ell_{1}\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm whose basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\), and let \(T\colon X(\ell_{1})\to X(\ell_{1})\) be an operator. Then the following hold:

  1. (a)

    For every \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), the set

    \(\{r\in\mathbb{N}:\exists s\in\mathbb{N}\text{ such that }|e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)}|\geqslant\varepsilon\}\)

    is finite.

  2. (b)

    For every \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), the set

    \(\{(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}:|e^{*}_{(r,s)}Te_{(i,j)}|\geqslant\varepsilon\}\)

    is finite.

  3. (c)

    For every \(r\in\mathbb{N}\), every infinite set \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\), every \(\varepsilon>0\), every finite set \(\{i_{1},\dots,i_{K}\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and every choice of infinite sets \(M_{1},\dots,M_{K}\subseteq\mathbb{N}\), there exists \(s\in M\) such that

    \(\{m\in M_{k}:|e^{*}_{(r,s)}Te_{(i_{k},m)}|\leqslant\varepsilon\}\)

    is infinite for every \(k=1,\dots,K\).

Let \(S\colon X(\ell_{1})\to X(\ell_{1})\) be an operator. Suppose that, for every \(r,i\in\mathbb{N}\),

\(\sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{s=1}^{\infty}|e^{*}_{(r,s)}Se_{(i,j)}|\leqslant\varepsilon 2^{-(r+i)}.\)

Then \(\lVert S\rVert\leqslant\varepsilon\).

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm whose basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\), and let \(T\colon X(\ell_{1})\to X(\ell_{1})\) be an operator. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist a strictly increasing sequence \((n_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\) and infinite sets \(M_{i}=\{m_{i}^{j}:j\in\mathbb{N}\}\), with \(m_{i}^{1}<m_{i}^{2}<\ldots\) for every \(i\), such that

\(|e^{*}_{(n_{r},m_{r}^{s})}Te_{(n_{i},m_{i}^{j})}|\leqslant\varepsilon 2^{-(r+i+s)}\qquad((r,s)\neq(i,j)).\)
Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm whose basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\). Then \(X(\ell_{1})\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.
The space \(c_{0}(\ell_{1})\) and the spaces \(\ell_{p}(\ell_{1})\), \(1<p<\infty\), are primary.

Let \((x_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) be a sequence in \(\ell_{\infty}\) and suppose that there exists \(K>0\) such that, for every finite set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and every scalar family \((\lambda_{n})_{n\in F}\),

\(\lVert\sum_{n\in F}\lambda_{n}x_{n}\rVert\leqslant K\max_{n\in F}|\lambda_{n}|.\)

Then the following hold:

  1. (a)

    For every \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}e^{*}_{m}x_{n}=0\).

  2. (b)

    For every \(\varepsilon>0\), every infinite set \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and every \(N_{0}\in\mathbb{N}\), there exists \(n\in M\) with \(n>N_{0}\) such that \(M\setminus M(x_{n},\varepsilon)\) is infinite.

Let \((x_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\ell_{\infty}\) be a sequence of vectors and suppose that there exists \(K>0\) such that, for every finite set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and every scalar family \((\lambda_{n})_{n\in F}\),

(3.3) \(\lVert\sum_{n\in F}\lambda_{n}x_{n}\rVert\leqslant K\max_{n\in F}|\lambda_{n}|.\)

Then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \((n_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\) such that

\(\sum_{j\not=k}|e_{n_{k}}^{*}x_{n_{j}}|<\varepsilon\quad\text{ for all }k\in\mathbb{N}.\)

Let \(T\colon\ell_{\infty}\to\ell_{\infty}\) be an operator. Then there exists an infinite subset \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that for all \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and all \(x=(x(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\in\ell_{\infty}(M)\) we have

\(e_{m}^{*}Tx=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}}x(n)(e_{m}^{*}Te_{n}).\)

Let \(T\colon\ell_{\infty}\to\ell_{\infty}\). Then there exists an infinite subset \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that \(P_{M}T|_{\ell_{\infty}(M)}\colon\ell_{\infty}(M)\to\ell_{\infty}(M)\) is weak∗-to-weak∗ continuous, where \(\ell_{\infty}(M)\) is seen as the dual space of \(\ell_{1}(M)\).
The space \(\ell_{\infty}\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm whose basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\), and let \(T\colon X(\ell_{\infty})\to X(\ell_{\infty})\) be an operator. Then the following hold:

  1. (a)

    For every \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), the set

    \(\{(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}:|e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)}|>\varepsilon\}\)

    is finite.

  2. (b)

    For every \(r\in\mathbb{N}\), every infinite set \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\), every \(\varepsilon>0\), every finite set \(\{i_{1},\dots,i_{K}\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}\), every choice of infinite sets \(M_{1},\dots,M_{K}\subseteq\mathbb{N}\), and every \(N_{0}\in\mathbb{N}\), there exists \(s\in M\) with \(s>N_{0}\) such that

    \(M_{k}\setminus M((r,s),i_{k},\varepsilon)\)

    is infinite for every \(k=1,\dots,K\).

  3. (c)

    For every \((r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\) we have

    \(\lim_{i\to\infty}\sup_{j\in\mathbb{N}}|e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)}|=0.\)

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm whose basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\), and let \(T\colon X(\ell_{\infty})\to X(\ell_{\infty})\) be an operator. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist a strictly increasing sequence \((n_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\) and infinite sets \(M_{i}=\{m_{i}^{j}:j\in\mathbb{N}\}\), with \(m_{i}^{1}<m_{i}^{2}<\cdots\), such that for every \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\),

\(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\\ (r,s)\neq(i,j)\end{subarray}}|e_{(n_{i},m_{i}^{j})}^{*}Te_{(n_{r},m_{r}^{s})}|<\varepsilon 2^{-i}.\)

Let \(T\colon X(\ell_{\infty})\to X(\ell_{\infty})\) be an operator. Then for any \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\) and any \(x=(x_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\in X(\ell_{\infty})\) we have

\(\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}}|(e^{*}_{(r,s)}x)(e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)})|\leqslant\lVert T\rVert\lVert x\rVert.\)

In particular \(\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}}(e^{*}_{(r,s)}x)(e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)})\) is absolutely summable.

Let \(T\colon X(\ell_{\infty})\to X(\ell_{\infty})\) be an operator. Then there exists an infinite subset \(M\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that, for all \(x\in X(\ell_{\infty}(M))\) and every \((i,j)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\),

\(e^{*}_{(i,j)}Tx=\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathbb{N}^{2}}(e^{*}_{(r,s)}x)(e^{*}_{(i,j)}Te_{(r,s)}).\)

Let \(X\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis and symmetric norm, and assume that this basis is not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}\). Then \(X(\ell_{\infty})\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.
The space \(c_{0}(\ell_{\infty})\) is primary.

results.title: (Primariness of \(\ell_{p}\)- and \(c_{0}\)-sums).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(\Gamma\) be an uncountable set with \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\).

  1. (i)

    Let \(Y\) be a WCG Banach space and suppose that \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\). Put

    \(X_{1}=\ell_{1}(\mathbb{N},Y).\)

    Assume that either

    1. (U)

      \(X_{1}\) is uniformly primary;

    2. (CF)

      \(X_{1}\) is primary and \(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)>\omega\).

    Then \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma,Y)\) is primary, and uniformly primary in case (i).

  2. (iv)

    Let \(Y\) be separable. For \(1<p<\infty\), put

    \(X_{p}=\ell_{p}(\mathbb{N},Y),\)

    and put \(X_{0}=c_{0}(\mathbb{N},Y)\). If the corresponding countable model \(X_{p}\), respectively \(X_{0}\), is uniformly primary, then \(\ell_{p}(\Gamma,Y)\), respectively \(c_{0}(\Gamma,Y)\), is uniformly primary. If the corresponding countable model is primary and \(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)>\omega\), then the corresponding uncountable sum is primary.

The results below distinguish two mechanisms. The two-sided countability mechanism applies to sums of separable spaces, over scalar bases not equivalent to \(\ell_{1}\), and works in ZFC for every uncountable \(\Gamma\). The one-sided mechanism applies to WCG \(\ell_{1}\)-sums and to certain non-separable coefficient spaces; it requires \(\left|\Gamma\right|>\omega_{1}\). Thus, for continuum-indexed WCG sums, the hypothesis becomes exactly \(\neg\mathrm{CH}\).

results.title: (Primary factorisation property).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(\Gamma\) be an uncountable set with \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\), and let \(X\) be a Banach space. Assume that one of the following holds:

  1. (UF)

    \(X\) has the uniform primary factorisation property;

  2. (CF)

    \(X\) has the primary factorisation property and \(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)>\omega\).

Then the following assertions hold.

  1. (i)

    If \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\) and \(X\) is WCG, then \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\) has the primary factorisation property, uniformly in case (UF).

  2. (ii)

    Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\). If \(X\) is separable, then \(E(\Gamma,X)\) has the primary factorisation property, uniformly in case (UF). This part has no cardinal assumption beyond the uncountability of \(\Gamma\).

  3. (iii)

    Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\). If \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\) and \(X^{*}\) contains a countable total set, then \(E(\Gamma,X)\) has the primary factorisation property, uniformly in case (UF).

The space \(\ell_{\infty}(\Gamma,X)\) is not covered by the arguments below: its canonical unit vectors do not form a Schauder basis in the sense used here, and the countable-support lemmas fail in that setting. We therefore make no assertion about \(\ell_{\infty}\)-sums in this section.

In the parts of Theorem 4.3 where \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\), the WCG assumption in the \(\ell_{1}\)-case may be replaced by the requirement that every operator \(S\colon X\to\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\) has separable range. Likewise, in the non-\(\ell_{1}\) \(E\)-sum case one may replace the countable-total-set assumption by the requirement that every operator \(S\colon X\to E\) has separable range. In both replacements one uses the one-sided outgoing-coordinate alternative in Lemma 4.27, and therefore the assumption \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\) remains essential for this proof. The ZFC separable-coefficient part of Theorem 4.3(ii) uses a different, two-sided argument.

results.title: (WCG \(\ell_{1}\)-sums at the continuum under \(\neg\mathrm{CH}\)).
results.statementHtml: Assume \(\neg\mathrm{CH}\), and let \(Y\) be a WCG Banach space. Put \(\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_{0}}\). If \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{N},Y)\) is uniformly primary, then \(\ell_{1}(\mathfrak{c},Y)\) is uniformly primary. If \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{N},Y)\) is primary, then \(\ell_{1}(\mathfrak{c},Y)\) is primary.
Assume \(\neg\mathrm{CH}\). Then the space \(\mathcal{M}[0,1]=C[0,1]^{*}\) is primary.

Corollary 4.7 is not a ZFC consequence of the present direct-sum argument. The representation

\(C[0,1]^{*}\simeq\ell_{1}(2^{\aleph_{0}},L_{1}[0,1])\)

writes \(C[0,1]^{*}\) as an \(\ell_{1}\)-sum of separable spaces, but separability of the coefficient space does not give the two-sided countability needed in Proposition 4.22. Indeed, if \(X\neq\{0\}\), choose \(x_{0}\in X\) and \(x_{0}^{*}\in X^{*}\) with \(x_{0}^{*}(x_{0})=1\). For a fixed \(\eta_{0}\in\Gamma\), the formula

\(R_{\eta_{0}}T((x_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma})=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}x_{0}^{*}(x_{\gamma})x_{0},\qquad R_{\eta}T=0\quad(\eta\neq\eta_{0}),\)

defines a bounded operator on \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\), and

\(R_{\eta_{0}}TR_{\gamma}\neq 0\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma).\)

Thus a single target coordinate may receive non-zero contributions from all source coordinates. This is precisely the one-sided phenomenon in the \(\ell_{1}\)-case, and at \(2^{\aleph_{0}}=\omega_{1}\) the Hajnal argument cannot be applied. A ZFC proof of the primariness of \(C[0,1]^{*}\), if one is available, would therefore have to use additional structure of \(C[0,1]^{*}\), not merely the above \(\ell_{1}(2^{\aleph_{0}},L_{1}[0,1])\) decomposition.

Let \(\Gamma\) be an uncountable set, let \(X\) be a separable Banach space with the UPFP, and let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\). Then \(E(\Gamma,X)\) has the UPFP. In particular, \(\ell_{p}(\Gamma,X)\), \(1<p<\infty\), and \(c_{0}(\Gamma,X)\) have the UPFP.

Let \(\alpha\) be an ordinal.

  1. (i)

    If \(\left|\Gamma\right|>\omega_{1}\) and \(1\leqslant p<\infty\), then \(\ell_{p}(\Gamma,C(\alpha))\) has the uniform primary factorisation property. In particular, it is primary.

  2. (ii)

    If \(\alpha<\omega_{1}\), \(\Gamma\) is uncountable, and \(1<p<\infty\), then \(\ell_{p}(\Gamma,C(\alpha))\) has the uniform primary factorisation property. The same is true of \(c_{0}(\Gamma,C(\alpha))\).

The \(\ell_{1}\)-case for separable coefficient spaces is not included in the ZFC statement above. Even for scalar coefficients, a bounded functional on \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\) may depend on all coordinates, so the incoming interaction sets need not be countable. This is exactly why the WCG \(\ell_{1}\)-results are stated under the one-sided hypothesis \(\left|\Gamma\right|>\omega_{1}\), and why continuum-indexed WCG applications are stated under \(\neg\mathrm{CH}\).
Let \(X\) be a Banach space. Then every \(x\in E(\Gamma,X)\) has countable support.

results.title: (Separable sets have countable support).
results.statementHtml: If \(Y\subseteq E(\Gamma,X)\) is separable, then there exists a countable \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(Y\subseteq E(\Delta,X)\).

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\), and let \(X\) be a Banach space. Assume that for every bounded operator \(S\colon X\to E\) there exists a countable set \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(S(X)\subseteq E(\Lambda)\). Then, for every bounded operator \(T\colon X\to E(\Gamma,X)\) there exists a countable set \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(T(X)\subseteq E(\Lambda,X)\).

results.title: (Support reduction).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\), let \(X\) be a Banach space, and let

\(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to E(\Gamma,X)\)

be a bounded operator. Assume that every bounded operator \(S\colon X\to E\) has separable range. Then, for every countable set \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\), there exists a countable set \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) such that

\(T(E(\Delta,X))\subseteq E(\Lambda,X).\)

results.title: (Support reduction).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\), let \(X\) be a Banach space, and let

\(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to E(\Gamma,X)\)

be a bounded operator. Assume that one of the following holds:

  1. (1)

    \(X\) is separable;

  2. (2)

    \(E=\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\) and \(X\) is WCG.

Then, for every countable set \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\), there exists a countable set \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) such that

\(T(E(\Delta,X))\subseteq E(\Lambda,X).\)

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\), and let \(X\) be a Banach space. Then for every \(x^{*}\in X^{*}\) and every bounded operator \(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to X\) there exists a countable set \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) such that

\(x^{*}TR_{\gamma}=0\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma\setminus\Delta).\)

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\), and let \(X\) be a Banach space which admits a countable total set \(M\subseteq X^{*}\). Then for every bounded operator \(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to X\), there exists a countable set \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) such that

\(TR_{\gamma}=0\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma\setminus\Delta).\)

results.title: (Countable blocks).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(Y\) be a Banach space and \(\Delta\) a non-empty countable set.

  1. (a)

    If \(1\leqslant p<\infty\) and \(X=\ell_{p}(\mathbb{N},Y)\), then \(\ell_{p}(\Delta,X)\) is linearly isometric to \(X\).

  2. (b)

    If \(X=c_{0}(\mathbb{N},Y)\), then \(c_{0}(\Delta,X)\) is linearly isometric to \(X\).

results.title: (Cofinality pigeonhole).
results.statementHtml: Let \(\kappa\) be an infinite cardinal with \(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)>\omega\), and let \(S\) be a set with \(\left|S\right|=\kappa\). If \(S=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}S_{n}\), then \(\left|S_{n}\right|=\kappa\) for some \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).

results.title: (Hajnal’s set mapping theorem).
results.statementHtml: Let \(\kappa\) be an infinite cardinal and let \(\lambda<\kappa\) be a cardinal. Let \(F\colon\kappa\to[\kappa]^{<\lambda}\) be a set mapping (i.e., \(\alpha\notin F(\alpha)\) for all \(\alpha\)). Then there exists \(H\subseteq\kappa\) with \(\left|H\right|=\kappa\) such that for all distinct \(\alpha,\beta\in H\) one has \(\alpha\notin F(\beta)\) and \(\beta\notin F(\alpha)\).

results.title: (Two-sided countable free set).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(\kappa\) be an uncountable cardinal and let

\(F\colon\kappa\to[\kappa]^{\leqslant\omega}\)

be a set mapping. Assume, in addition, that every inverse fibre

\(F^{-1}(\{\alpha\})=\{\beta<\kappa:\alpha\in F(\beta)\}\)

is countable. Then there is \(H\subseteq\kappa\) with \(\left|H\right|=\kappa\) such that, for all distinct \(\alpha,\beta\in H\),

\(\alpha\notin F(\beta)\qquad\text{and}\qquad\beta\notin F(\alpha).\)

The one-sided countable-valued hypothesis is not enough at \(\kappa=\omega_{1}\). Indeed, the map \(F(\alpha)=\{\beta:\beta<\alpha\}\) on \(\omega_{1}\) is countable-valued and has no two-point free set. Thus every use below of Hajnal’s theorem with merely countable values is made under the explicit assumption \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\), unless a two-sided countability hypothesis is available.

Let \(X\) be a WCG Banach space, let \(P\colon\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\to\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\) be a bounded projection, and put \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\). Then there exist pairwise disjoint countable sets \((\Gamma_{\alpha})_{\alpha<\kappa}\) with

\(\Gamma=\bigsqcup_{\alpha<\kappa}\Gamma_{\alpha}\)

such that the following hold.

  1. (i)

    for each \(\alpha<\kappa\),

    \(P(\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X))\subseteq\ell_{1}\Bigl(\bigcup_{\beta\leqslant\alpha}\Gamma_{\beta},X\Bigr);\)
  2. (ii)

    for each \(\alpha<\kappa\), the operator

    \(Q_{\alpha}:=R_{\Gamma_{\alpha}}P|_{\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)}\colon\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)\to\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)\)

    is a bounded projection;

  3. (iii)

    the set mapping

    \(F(\alpha)=\Bigl\{\beta<\alpha:\ R_{\Gamma_{\beta}}P|_{\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)}\neq 0\Bigr\}\)

    takes countable values.

results.title: (A large diagonal family).
results.statementHtml:
With notation as in Lemma 4.24, assume in addition that \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\). Then there exists \(H\subseteq\kappa\) with \(\left|H\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\Gamma_{\beta}}P(\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X))=\{0\}\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in H,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)

In particular, on the subspace

\(W=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{\alpha\in H}\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)\Bigr)_{\ell_{1}(H)}\subseteq\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X),\)

the operator \(P\) is diagonal: if \(w=\sum_{\beta\in H}x_{\beta}\in W\), with \(x_{\beta}\in\ell_{1}(\Gamma_{\beta},X)\), then

\(R_{\Gamma_{\alpha}}Pw=Q_{\alpha}x_{\alpha}\qquad(\alpha\in H).\)

Let \(X\) be a separable Banach space, and let \(E_{0}(\Gamma,X)\) be either \(\ell_{p}(\Gamma,X)\), \(1<p<\infty\), or \(c_{0}(\Gamma,X)\). If \(P\colon E_{0}(\Gamma,X)\to E_{0}(\Gamma,X)\) is a bounded projection, then there are pairwise disjoint countable sets \((\Gamma_{\alpha})_{\alpha<\kappa}\) partitioning \(\Gamma\), block projections

\(Q_{\alpha}=R_{\Gamma_{\alpha}}P|_{E_{0}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X)},\)

and a set \(H\subseteq\kappa\) with \(\left|H\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\Gamma_{\beta}}P(E_{0}(\Gamma_{\alpha},X))=\{0\}\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in H,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)

results.title: (Coordinate diagonalisation).
results.statementHtml:
As in this section, Γ is uncountable.

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\), let \(X\) be a Banach space, let

\(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to E(\Gamma,X)\)

be bounded, and put \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\). Assume that one of the following two alternatives holds.

  1. (a)

    \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\), and at least one of the two sets

    \(\{\eta\in\Gamma:\ R_{\eta}TR_{\gamma}\neq 0\},\qquad\{\eta\in\Gamma:\ R_{\gamma}TR_{\eta}\neq 0\}\)

    is countable for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\).

  2. (b)

    Both sets

    \(\{\eta\in\Gamma:\ R_{\eta}TR_{\gamma}\neq 0\},\qquad\{\eta\in\Gamma:\ R_{\gamma}TR_{\eta}\neq 0\}\)

    are countable for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\).

Then there exists \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(\left|\Lambda\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\beta}TR_{\alpha}=0\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\Lambda,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)
Correction in this reading edition

The section assumes an uncountable index set. This hypothesis is now explicit in the statement; without it, the countable c₀ example disproves the isolated formulation.

Let \(X\) be a WCG Banach space, let \(T\colon\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\to\ell_{1}(\Gamma,X)\) be bounded, and put \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\). Assume that \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\). Then there exists \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(\left|\Lambda\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\beta}TR_{\alpha}=0\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\Lambda,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\), let \(X\) be a Banach space such that \(X^{*}\) contains a countable total set, let \(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to E(\Gamma,X)\) be bounded, and put \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\). Assume that \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\). Then there exists \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(\left|\Lambda\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\beta}TR_{\alpha}=0\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\Lambda,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)

As in this section, Γ is uncountable.

Let \(E\) be a Banach space with a symmetric basis \((e_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) not equivalent to the unit vector basis of \(\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\), let \(X\) be separable, and let

\(T\colon E(\Gamma,X)\to E(\Gamma,X)\)

be bounded. Put \(\kappa=\left|\Gamma\right|\). Then there exists \(\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(\left|\Lambda\right|=\kappa\) such that

\(R_{\beta}TR_{\alpha}=0\qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\Lambda,\ \alpha\neq\beta).\)
Correction in this reading edition

The uncountability convention from the section is explicit here, as required by the formal proof.

The separable-range variant mentioned in Remark 4.5 follows from the same proof. Let \(F\) denote the scalar coordinate space, so that \(F=\ell_{1}(\Gamma)\) in the \(\ell_{1}\)-case and \(F=E\) in the general symmetric-basis case. If \(\kappa>\omega_{1}\) and every operator \(S\colon X\to F\) has separable range, then Lemma 4.15, applied to one coordinate at a time, gives the outgoing-coordinate hypothesis in alternative (a) of Lemma 4.27; the rest of the proof of Theorem 4.3 is unchanged.
As in Theorem 3.8, iterated versions of Theorem 4.3 can be obtained. Since the argument is a routine adaptation of the ideas above, we omit the details.
The space \(\ell_{\infty}/c_{0}\cong C(\omega^{*})\) has the \(2\)-PFP.

Here X is assumed to be separable.

As noted in , if \(X\) has the PFP, then so does \(C(\omega^{*},X)\), and the same argument yields the corresponding statement for the UPFP.

Correction in this reading edition

The cited transfer requires separability of X. The corrected separable version is proved in Lean with the same factorisation constant.

Let \(E\) be a Banach space and let \(S\colon E\to E\) be bounded. Assume that there exist complemented subspaces \(Y,Z\subseteq E\) and an isomorphism \(V\colon E\to Y\) such that \(S|_{Y}\colon Y\to Z\) is an isomorphism. Then \(\mathrm{Id}_{E}\) factors through \(S\).

For every \(1<p<\infty\), the space \(JT_{p}\) has the uniform primary factorisation property. That is, there exists a constant \(C_{p}\geqslant 1\) such that for every bounded operator \(T\colon JT_{p}\to JT_{p}\) there are \(U,V\in\mathscr{B}(JT_{p})\) with either \(UTV=\mathrm{Id}_{JT_{p}}\) or \(U(\mathrm{Id}_{JT_{p}}-T)V=\mathrm{Id}_{JT_{p}}\) and \(\|U\|\,\|V\|\leqslant C_{p}\).

For context, Blower’s theorem that \(\mathcal{B}(\ell_{2})\) is primary and Wark’s primariness results for certain \(\ell_{\infty}\)-direct sums are formulated in terms of projections and decompositions. They therefore do not, at least not directly, yield the PFP or the UPFP. The argument below for \(\mathcal{B}(\ell_{p})\) is instead genuinely operator-theoretic.

Let \(N\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(I,J\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}\) be finite non-empty sets. Then for unimodular scalars \((\varepsilon_{i})_{i\in I}\) and \((\delta_{j})_{j\in J}\):

\(\lVert\sum_{i\in I}\varepsilon_{i}e_{ij_{0}}\rVert=|I|^{1/p}\quad(\text{fixed }j_{0}),\qquad\lVert\sum_{j\in J}\delta_{j}e_{i_{0}j}\rVert=|J|^{1/q}\quad(\text{fixed }i_{0}).\)

results.title: (Finite-dimensional scalarisation).
results.statementHtml:
Fix \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(K\geqslant 1\) and \(0<\varepsilon<\tfrac{1}{4}\). There exists \(N_{0}=N_{0}(n,K,\varepsilon,p)\in\mathbb{N}\) such that whenever \(N\geqslant N_{0}\) and \(T\in\mathcal{B}(X_{N})\) with \(\lVert T\rVert\leqslant K\), there exist disjoint subsets \(\alpha,\tau\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}\) with \(|\alpha|=|\tau|=n\) and a scalar \(c\in\mathbb{C}\) such that

\(\lVert K_{\alpha,\tau}\,T\,J_{\alpha,\tau}-c\,\mathrm{Id}_{X_{n}}\rVert<\varepsilon.\)

Consequently, one of \(K_{\alpha,\tau}TJ_{\alpha,\tau}\) and \(K_{\alpha,\tau}(\mathrm{Id}_{X_{N}}-T)J_{\alpha,\tau}\) is invertible on \(X_{n}\) and its inverse has norm at most \(4\).

Let \(N\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(A\in X_{N}\). Put \(a=\big|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\big|<\frac{1}{2}\). Then

\(\lVert A\rVert_{HS}\leqslant N^{\frac{1}{2}+a}\,\lVert A\rVert.\)

Moreover, if \(B\in X_{k}\) then \(\lVert B\rVert\leqslant k^{a}\lVert B\rVert_{HS}\).

results.title: (Block projection lemma).
results.statementHtml:
Fix \(k,d\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). There exists \(N_{0}=N_{0}(k,d,\varepsilon,p)\in\mathbb{N}\) such that for all \(N\geqslant N_{0}\) and every \(d\)-dimensional subspace \(E\subseteq X_{N}\) there exist subsets \(\alpha,\tau\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}\) with \(|\alpha|=|\tau|=k\) such that the block projection \(Q_{\alpha,\tau}=J_{\alpha,\tau}K_{\alpha,\tau}\) satisfies

\(\lVert Q_{\alpha,\tau}x\rVert\leqslant\varepsilon\lVert x\rVert\qquad(x\in E).\)

Let \(F\) be finite-dimensional, let \(S\colon\mathcal{M}_{p}\to F\) be bounded, and let \(J\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) be infinite. Then for every \(\eta>0\) there exists an infinite set \(I\subseteq J\) such that \(\|SP_{I}\|<\eta\).

results.title: (Almost diagonalisation).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(T\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}_{p})\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). There exist contractions \(A,B\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}_{p})\) with \(AB=\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal{M}_{p}}\) and an operator

\(T^{\prime}=ATB\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}_{p})\)

such that \(\lVert T^{\prime}-D\rVert<\varepsilon\) for a diagonal operator \(D=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{\infty}D_{k}\). Moreover, \(T^{\prime}\) factors through \(T\) and \(\mathrm{Id}-T^{\prime}\) factors through \(\mathrm{Id}-T\) (via the same \(A,B\)).

Let \((n_{j})_{j\geqslant 1}\) be strictly increasing with \(n_{j}\geqslant j\). Then the coordinate subspace of \(\mathcal{M}_{p}\) supported on \(\{n_{j}:j\geqslant 1\}\) contains a \(1\)-complemented copy of \(\mathcal{M}_{p}\).

results.title: (Diagonal case).
results.statementHtml: Let \(D=\bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty}D_{n}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}_{p})\) be diagonal. Then there exist \(U,V\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}_{p})\) such that either \(UDV=\mathrm{Id}\) or \(U(\mathrm{Id}-D)V=\mathrm{Id}\) and \(\lVert U\rVert\lVert V\rVert\leqslant 4\).
For every \(p\in(1,\infty)\) the space \(\mathcal{M}_{p}\) has the \(8\)-primary factorisation property.
For every \(p\in(1,\infty)\) the Banach space \(\mathcal{B}(\ell_{p})\) has the uniform primary factorisation property.

Let \(K\geqslant 1\). A subset \(A\subseteq\Gamma\) is called a \(K\)-copying set for \(\mathcal{F}\) if

\(X_{\mathcal{F}}(A)\simeq_{K}X_{\mathcal{F}}.\)

Let \(K\geqslant 1\). We say that \(\mathcal{F}\) is \(K\)-primary under sums if, for every partition \(\Gamma=\Gamma_{0}\sqcup\Gamma_{1}\), at least one of \(\Gamma_{0}\) and \(\Gamma_{1}\) contains a \(K\)-copying set for \(\mathcal{F}\).

Let \(D\geqslant 1\). We say that \(\mathcal{F}\) is \(D\)-diagonalisable if, for every \(T\in\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathcal{F}})\) and every \(\eta>0\), there are \(A\subseteq\Gamma\), an isomorphism

\(J\colon X_{\mathcal{F}}\longrightarrow X_{\mathcal{F}}(A),\qquad R=J^{-1}\colon X_{\mathcal{F}}(A)\longrightarrow X_{\mathcal{F}},\)

with \(\|J\|\,\|R\|\leqslant D,\) and a function \(a\in\ell_{\infty}(\Gamma)\) such that

\(\|RP_{A}TJ-M_{a}\|<\eta.\)
Let \(K,D\geqslant 1\). We say that \(\mathcal{F}\) is \((K,D)\)-primary for factorisation if it is \(K\)-primary under sums and \(D\)-diagonalisable.

Let \(\mathcal{F}\) be a \((K,D)\)-primary filter for factorisation on \(\Gamma\). Then

\(X_{\mathcal{F}}=c_{\mathcal{F}}(\Gamma)\)

has the \((2KD)^{+}\)-primary factorisation property. In particular, \(X_{\mathcal{F}}\) has the UPFP.

Let \(B\subseteq\Gamma\). We say that \(B\) contains a coordinate copy of \(\mathcal{F}\) if there are \(C\subseteq B\) and a bijection \(\theta\colon\Gamma\to C\) such that, for every \(A\subseteq\Gamma\),

\(A\in\mathcal{F}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\theta(A)\cup(\Gamma\setminus C)\in\mathcal{F}.\)

Equivalently, the trace filter \(\mathcal{F}_{C}\) is isomorphic to \(\mathcal{F}\).
Let \(\kappa=|\Gamma|\). We say that \(\mathcal{F}\) is large-set self-similar if every subset \(B\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(|B|=\kappa\) contains a coordinate copy of \(\mathcal{F}\).

results.title: (Rosenthal’s lemma).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(\Gamma\) be an infinite set, and let \((\mu_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\) be a uniformly bounded family of finitely additive scalar measures on \(\Gamma\). Suppose that \(\mu_{\gamma}(\{\gamma\})=0\) for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\). Then, for every \(\eta>0\), there is \(A\subseteq\Gamma\) with \(|A|=|\Gamma|\) such that

\(|\mu_{\gamma}|(A)<\eta\qquad(\gamma\in A).\)
If \(\mathcal{F}\) is large-set self-similar, then \(\mathcal{F}\) is \((1,1)\)-primary for factorisation. Consequently, \(X_{\mathcal{F}}\) has the \(2^{+}\)-primary factorisation property.

Let \(\kappa=|\Gamma|\), and let \(\mu\leqslant\kappa\) be an infinite cardinal. Define

\(\mathcal{F}_{\mu}=\{A\subseteq\Gamma:|\Gamma\setminus A|<\mu\}.\)

Then \(\mathcal{F}_{\mu}\) is large-set self-similar. Indeed, if \(B\subseteq\Gamma\) has cardinality \(\kappa\), then the trace filter on \(B\) is

\((\mathcal{F}_{\mu})_{B}=\{C\subseteq B:|B\setminus C|<\mu\},\)

which is isomorphic to \(\mathcal{F}_{\mu}\) through any bijection \(\Gamma\to B\). Hence \(c_{\mathcal{F}_{\mu}}(\Gamma)\) has the \(2^{+}\)-PFP.

For \(\mu=\omega\), this recovers the usual cofinite-filter case \(c_{\mathcal{F}_{\omega}}(\Gamma)=c_{0}(\Gamma)\). For \(\mu=\omega_{1}\), it gives the co-countable-filter case \(c_{\mathcal{F}_{\omega_{1}}}(\Gamma)=\ell_{\infty}^{c}(\Gamma)\), whenever \(|\Gamma|\geqslant\omega_{1}\), which recovers .

Definition 6.3 should therefore be read as an abstract operator criterion, not as the primary source of examples. The set-theoretic condition in Definition 6.7 is stronger but much easier to verify: Rosenthal’s lemma turns large-set self-similarity into diagonalisation, and large set self-similarity also gives the required primariness under sums. Thus one obtains the concrete implication

\(\text{large-set self-similar filter}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c_{\mathcal{F}}(\Gamma)\text{ has the }2^{+}\text{-PFP}.\)

results.title: (Primariness does not imply PFP).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(X_{\mathrm{GM}}\) denote the prime Gowers–Maurey space, see . Then \(X_{\mathrm{GM}}\) is prime, hence primary. On the other hand, for this space the quotient of \(\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\) by the ideal of strictly singular operators is isomorphic, as a Banach algebra, to \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{Z})\) equipped with the convolution product. Let

\(q\colon\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\to\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})/\mathcal{SS}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\cong\ell_{1}(\mathbb{Z})\)

denote the quotient map. For every maximal ideal \(M\) of \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{Z})\), the preimage \(q^{-1}(M)\) is a maximal ideal of \(\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\); in fact, these are all the maximal ideals of \(\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\), since every maximal ideal of \(\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\) contains the ideal of strictly singular operators. Since the maximal ideal space of \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{Z})\) is naturally identified with the unit circle \(\mathbb{T}\), the algebra \(\ell_{1}(\mathbb{Z})\) has continuum many maximal ideals. Hence \(\mathcal{B}(X_{\mathrm{GM}})\) has continuum many maximal ideals. By Proposition 2.6, it follows that \(X_{\mathrm{GM}}\) cannot have the PFP. Thus, primariness does not imply the PFP.
Does every Banach space with the PFP have to be primary?
Is every Banach space with a symmetric basis primary?
Does there exist a Banach space with the PFP but without the UPFP?
Let \(X\) be a primary Banach space. Must \(X^{*}\) be primary? What if \(X\) has the PFP or the UPFP? Do either of these properties pass to the dual space?

To what extent can the arguments for uncountable sums be pushed back to the countable setting? For example, can the uncountable methods be adapted to recover the PFP or UPFP for difficult countable mixed sums, spaces such as \(C(\alpha,\ell_{p})\) or related bi-parameter spaces?
Can the constants in Appendix A be improved substantially, especially in the square case or in the \(c_{0}\)/\(\ell_{p}\)-stable case?

results.title: (A quantitative form of Pełczyński’s decomposition method).
results.statementHtml:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be Banach spaces such that

  1. (i)

    \(X\) has a \(C_{1}\)-complemented subspace \(E\) which is \(C_{2}\)-isomorphic to \(Y\);

  2. (ii)

    \(Y\) has a \(C_{3}\)-complemented subspace \(G\) which is \(C_{4}\)-isomorphic to \(X\).

Suppose further that either

  1. (a)

    there exists \(1\leqslant r\leqslant\infty\) such that

    \(X\simeq_{C_{5}}X\oplus_{r}X\qquad\text{and}\qquad Y\simeq_{C_{6}}Y\oplus_{r}Y,\)

    or

  2. (b)
    \(X\simeq_{C_{5}}c_{0}(X)\qquad\text{or}\qquad X\simeq_{C_{5}}\ell_{p}(X)\)

    for some \(1\leqslant p\leqslant\infty\).

Then there exists a constant \(C\geqslant 1\), depending only on \(C_{1},\dots,C_{6}\) in case (a), and only on \(C_{1},\dots,C_{5}\) in case (b), such that \(X\simeq_{C}Y\). Moreover, the proof below gives an explicit admissible choice of \(C\).

In case (a), the choice of the norm on the two-fold direct sums is only a normalisation. One may equally work with the max-norm, as in , or with any other standard norm on a finite direct sum; the resulting formulation is equivalent, with constants changing by a factor depending only on that choice.

Let \(X\) be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Suppose that \(X\) contains a complemented subspace \(E\) such that

\(E\simeq E\oplus\mathbb{K}.\)

Then \(X\simeq X\oplus\mathbb{K}\). In particular, \(X\) is isomorphic to each of its hyperplanes.

Let \(X\) be quasi-reflexive of order one. Then \(X^{*}\) is quasi-reflexive of order one. Moreover, if \(X=Y\oplus Z\), then

\(X^{**}/\kappa_{X}(X)\simeq\bigl(Y^{**}/\kappa_{Y}(Y)\bigr)\oplus\bigl(Z^{**}/\kappa_{Z}(Z)\bigr),\)

where \(\kappa_{X}\), \(\kappa_{Y}\), and \(\kappa_{Z}\) denote the canonical embeddings.

Let \(X\) be a quasi-reflexive Banach space of order one. Suppose that

  1. (i)

    \(X\) is primary;

  2. (ii)

    \(X\) is isomorphic to each of its hyperplanes;

  3. (iii)

    \(X^{*}\) is isomorphic to each of its hyperplanes.

Then \(X^{*}\) is primary.
Let \(1<p<\infty\). If \(J_{p}\) is primary, then \(J_{p}^{*}\) is primary. In particular, the dual of the classical James space \(J_{2}\) is primary.

The proof above uses primarity of \(J_{p}\) only as an input. For \(p=2\), this input is classical by . The remaining structural ingredients used here are the quasi-reflexivity of \(J_{p}\) of order one and the complemented \(\ell_{p}\)-subspace theorem for \(J_{p}\); both are recorded in . Notice that the dual hyperplane reduction uses the complemented copy of \(\ell_{q}\) obtained by dualising a projection onto a complemented copy of \(\ell_{p}\) in \(J_{p}\); the exact exponent is immaterial for the argument, since every \(\ell_{r}\) with \(1<r<\infty\) is isomorphic to its hyperplanes.

definition-2-1.note: The definition records an actual isomorphism of distortion at most C. The final sentence is corrected to an approximate bound: an infimum need not be attained. The linked theorem proves the equivalence with bounds C + ε for every ε > 0.

definition-2-2.note: The control is evaluated at max(1, ‖P‖), including the zero projection. This is the corrected convention used in the thesis.

theorem-2-3.note: Mutually complemented Banach spaces are isomorphic if both are isomorphic to their squares, or if the first is isomorphic to its c0 or lp sequence sum for some 1<=p<=infinity.

definition-2-4.note: The displayed definition is UPFP. It asks for one C ≥ 1 such that C-PFP holds for every operator. The same module defines PFP, C-PFP and C⁺-PFP.

proposition-2-5.note: Conjugate T by S, apply C-PFP in F, and conjugate both factors back. Each conjugation costs the distortion of S; their product gives C ||S||^2 ||S^-1||^2.

proposition-2-6.note: The statement here includes E ≠ {0}. This hypothesis is necessary: the printed equivalence fails for the zero space. The proof includes maximality and uniqueness.

remark-2-7.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

lemma-3-1.note: For a normalized unconditional Schauder basis, absence of any increasing subsequence with closed span isomorphic to ell1 is equivalent to weak nullity, and the rank-one argument identifies this with decay of every operator row.

lemma-3-2.note: An absolute geometric bound on every matrix entry first bounds the norm of each column, then bounds the operator norm using that each coordinate functional has norm one. Both inequalities pass finite-sum estimates to convergent Schauder expansions.

theorem-3-3.note: A symmetric normalized basis not equivalent to the ell_1 basis is weakly null. Both matrix directions can therefore be made geometrically small by a recursive subsequence choice. Finite permutation invariance and unconditionality construct contractive restriction and isometric insertion maps, extended from the dense algebraic span. Compression differs arbitrarily little from its bounded diagonal. On an infinite diagonal branch, reciprocals have modulus at most two. The Neumann correction gives every bound 2+epsilon.

remark-3-4.note: A normalized subsymmetric basis not equivalent to ell1 gives UPFP. Actual increasing-subsequence insertion and reading maps replace the isometric maps in the symmetric argument.

definition-3-5.note: This is the property that an operator is infinitely supported. It applies the recursive supporting-prefix condition to the diagonal coefficients of the iterated basis.

lemma-3-6.note: For each actual terminal vector, its own coordinate equals one. Therefore its diagonal entries for T and I-T add to one, so at least one has modulus at least one half. Backward induction and finite union of finite sets imply that one alternative has infinitely many supporting first-level nodes.

lemma-3-7.note: An infinitely supported operator admits an infinitely splitting subtree whose actual closed terminal span is isometric to the whole iterated space, all selected diagonal entries are at least one half, and some enumeration has the stated geometric off-diagonal estimates.

theorem-3-8.note: Every nonempty finite iteration X1(X2(...(Xn))) of Banach spaces with symmetric norms and symmetric bases not equivalent to the ell1 unit vector basis has 2-plus-PFP.

lemma-3-9.note: Choose N with N epsilon greater than the column-sum bound. Among N retained rows, each later column has a small entry. Infinite pigeonhole keeps one row small on an infinite tail. Iterate using nested infinite sets so every earlier estimate persists.

lemma-3-10.note: Every x in ell_1 is the sum of its scalar multiples of unit vectors. Apply T to this convergent sum and bound the norm by the sum of |x_i| times the column bound. This gives ||Tx|| <= epsilon ||x||.

theorem-3-11.note: Retain infinite sets on which each selected row has small future entries, and then cut a tail where the selected column has small total mass. Use delta_k=(eta/4)(1/2)^k. The old rows contribute at most eta/2 and the future rows less than eta/4. Coordinate compression is therefore within eta of its diagonal. On an infinite set, one diagonal branch factors with constant 2. The Neumann inverse changes this to any prescribed 2+epsilon.

lemma-3-12.note: For each fixed target, only finitely many source rows have a large entry anywhere in the row. For each fixed source, only finitely many target coordinates have a large entry. Given finitely many infinite source reservoirs and an infinite set of target candidates, one target candidate has small entries on an infinite subset of every source reservoir.

lemma-3-13.note: The exact supremum of the absolute column sums bounds each genuine ell1 block Q_r T J_i. Geometric summation of the block bounds, using the convergent inner and outer expansions and their norm estimates, gives operator norm at most epsilon.

lemma-3-14.note: Choose strictly increasing outer indices and a strictly increasing infinite inner sequence in each selected row. Every off-diagonal entry is at most epsilon/2^(r+i+s+3), with s the target inner index and no dependence on the source inner index. Recursively keep infinite source reservoirs on which all previously selected targets satisfy their budgets.

theorem-3-15.note: If X has a symmetric basis and symmetric norm and the basis is not equivalent to the ell1 unit vector basis, the genuine vector-valued sum X(ell1) has 2-plus-PFP.

corollary-3-16.note: The actual c0 sum of scalar ell1 is primary, and so is the actual lp sum of scalar ell1 for every 1<p<infinity.

lemma-3-17.note: A uniform bound on finite scalar combinations by K times the maximum coefficient implies that every fixed coordinate tends to zero along the vector sequence. Inside every infinite set and beyond every prescribed index, some vector is small on infinitely many coordinates of that set.

lemma-3-18.note: There is an increasing subsequence for which every off-diagonal absolute row sum is smaller than epsilon. Nested infinite sets preserve small old-source entries and a small total contribution from future sources.

proposition-3-19.note: Every bounded ell_infinity operator has an infinite coordinate support M on which every conclusion coordinate equals its absolutely convergent unit-vector matrix series. Every bounded vector supported in M is included, and the conclusion coordinate is unrestricted.

corollary-3-20.note: Every scalar ell_infinity operator has an infinite support M for which the actual coordinate compression on ell_infinity(M) is continuous from the usual ell1-predual weak-star topology to itself.

theorem-3-21.note: Scalar ell_infinity has 2-plus-PFP. After the representation restriction and a small-interference subsequence, canonical coordinate compression is arbitrarily close to its bounded diagonal part. An infinite large diagonal branch and a Neumann inverse give every factor bound 2+epsilon.

lemma-3-22.note: For a fixed conclusion coordinate, only finitely many source pairs have modulus above a positive threshold. Given finitely many infinite target reservoirs and an infinite source reservoir, a sufficiently late source coordinate preserves infinitely many small entries in every target reservoir. For a fixed source coordinate, the supremum norm of its image in outer row i tends to zero.

lemma-3-23.note: There are strictly increasing outer indices and increasing inner indices in every selected row so that every off-diagonal absolute row sum is smaller than epsilon times 2 to minus the positive target row index.

lemma-3-24.note: For every x and conclusion coordinate, the absolute weighted matrix series sums to at most the operator norm times the norm of x.

proposition-3-25.note: There is one infinite inner support M such that every conclusion coordinate of T x is its absolutely convergent weighted matrix series whenever every row of x is supported in M.

theorem-3-26.note: Under the symmetric non-ell1 basis hypothesis on X, the genuine vector-valued sum X(ell-infinity) has 2-plus-PFP.

corollary-3-27.note: The actual c0 sum of scalar ell_infinity is primary.

theorem-4-1.note: WCG ell_1 sums transfer primariness from the countable model for index cardinal greater than aleph_1. For separable coefficients, finite 1

remark-4-2.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

theorem-4-3.note: For WCG X and |Gamma|>aleph_1, factorisation transfers to ell_1(Gamma,X). For a symmetric non-ell1 scalar family, it transfers to the actual norm-series sum when X is separable and Gamma uncountable, or when X has a countable total dual set and |Gamma|>aleph_1. Uniform PFP gives both PFP and UPFP; ordinary PFP additionally requires uncountable cofinality.

remark-4-4.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

remark-4-5.note: If every coefficient-to-scalar-coordinate operator has separable range, outgoing coordinate supports are countable. Above aleph1, one-sided Hajnal selection supplies a full-cardinality diagonal coordinate set and the factorisation transfer follows.

corollary-4-6.note: Under anti-CH and WCG of X, primariness or uniform primariness of ell_1(N,X) transfers to the continuum-indexed ell_1 sum.

corollary-4-7.note: Under the original anti-CH hypothesis, the actual continuous dual of C[0,1] is primary, over every real or complex RCLike scalar field. Actual Lebesgue L1 has 4-PFP and is primary, as additional supporting results.

remark-4-8.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

corollary-4-9.note: For separable coefficients with UPFP and an uncountable index set, every symmetric non-ell1 norm-series sum has UPFP. In particular, every finite 1

corollary-4-10.note: Both original clauses of Corollary4.10 hold for the actual lp and c0 sums of ordinal continuous-function spaces. Clause(i) retains every ordinal coefficient, the source cardinal threshold, p=1 and every finite p; clause(ii) retains the original countability and uncountability hypotheses.

remark-4-11.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

lemma-4-12.note: The actual unconditionally summable expansion has countable support. Normalization identifies its support with the nonzero coordinate coefficients, and applying this to the scalar norm vector gives countable support of every vector in the full symmetric sum.

lemma-4-13.note: Take the union of coordinate supports over a countable dense set. It is countable. Each coordinate outside that union vanishes on the dense set, and continuity makes it vanish on its closure.

lemma-4-14.note: If every bounded map from X into the scalar basis space has a countable common coordinate support, then every map from X into the vector-valued sum also has such a support.

lemma-4-15.note: If every bounded map from X to the scalar basis space has separable range, each endomorphism of the vector-valued sum sends each countable-coordinate subspace into another countable-coordinate subspace.

corollary-4-16.note: Countable-coordinate support preservation holds for separable coefficients in general symmetric sums, and for WCG coefficients in ell1 sums.

lemma-4-17.note: For a symmetric non-ell1 sum and T into X, each scalar functional on X annihilates T on all but countably many singleton coordinates.

lemma-4-18.note: A countable total subset of the coefficient dual makes every bounded map from the non-ell1 sum to X vanish on all but countably many source coordinates.

lemma-4-19.note: A nonempty countable sum of ellp(N,Y) is linearly isometric to ellp(N,Y) for finite 1<=p. The corresponding c0 assertion holds as well.

lemma-4-20.note: A countable cover of a set of cardinality kappa has a member of cardinality kappa when cf(kappa)>aleph0.

proposition-4-21.note: For an infinite cardinal kappa and lambda<kappa, every set mapping with values of size strictly below lambda has a free subset of size kappa.

proposition-4-22.note: For every uncountable cardinal, a set mapping whose values and inverse incidence fibres are countable has a free subset of full cardinality.

remark-4-23.note: On omega1, the predecessor mapping has countable values, but every free set has at most one point.

lemma-4-24.note: A projection on an ell1 sum with WCG coefficients has a countable-block partition, is triangular in its initial-ordinal order, induces a projection on each diagonal block, and has countably many lower interactions per block.

lemma-4-25.note: Above aleph1, the triangular countable-block decomposition has a full-cardinality family of mutually noninteracting blocks. The displayed diagonal identity holds on every vector supported by their union.

lemma-4-26.note: The printed statement is proved, together with a version making the section’s uncountability convention explicit.

lemma-4-27.note: The section’s convention that Γ is uncountable is made explicit in this reading edition. The unrestricted countable version is false; Lean also contains a counterexample.

lemma-4-28.note: For WCG coefficients and index cardinal above aleph1, each endomorphism of the ell1 sum has a full-cardinality coordinate set on which all off-diagonal entries vanish.

lemma-4-29.note: For a symmetric non-ell1 sum above aleph1 and coefficients with a countable total dual set, each endomorphism has a full-cardinality set of pairwise vanishing off-diagonal entries.

lemma-4-30.note: The section’s uncountability hypothesis is explicit here and in Lean. Without it, the printed isolated statement fails on countable c₀.

remark-4-31.note: Apply the separable-range countable-support theorem separately to each scalar coordinate operator, then use the one-sided outgoing alternative of coordinate diagonalisation and the proved transfer assembly.

remark-4-32.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

proposition-5-1.note: The actual Banach quotient of bounded scalar sequences by sequences converging to zero has the endpoint 2-PFP.

remark-5-2.note: The corrected remark assumes that X is separable. The formal proof retains the factorisation constant. It makes no claim about the printed unrestricted transfer.

lemma-5-3.note: Let V map E isomorphically onto Y and W be the restriction of S onto Z. With a bounded projection P onto Z, choose U=V^-1 W^-1 P and the second factor inclusion_Y V. Their product with S is the identity.

theorem-5-4.note: For every finite 1<p, the actual completed James-tree space has UPFP. The manuscript finite-chain convention and the cited consecutive-segment convention are registered as separate targets.

remark-5-5.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

lemma-5-6.note: Column sums of unimodular matrix units have norm card(I)^(1/p), while row sums have norm card(J)^(1/q), where q=p/(p-1).

proposition-5-7.note: For each positive block size, K>=1 and 0<epsilon<1/4, sufficiently large finite matrix blocks admit disjoint row and column subsets on which compression of every operator of norm at most K is within epsilon of a scalar identity. One of the compressed operator and its complement has inverse norm at most four.

lemma-5-8.note: With a=abs(1/p-1/2)<1/2, the Hilbert-Schmidt norm is at most N^(1/2+a) times the operator norm; conversely the operator norm is at most k^a times the Hilbert-Schmidt norm.

lemma-5-9.note: For fixed positive k,d and 0<epsilon<1, sufficiently large matrix blocks admit a k-by-k block projection of norm at most epsilon on every prescribed d-dimensional operator subspace.

lemma-5-10.note: Every bounded map from the growing matrix product into a finite-dimensional normed space is arbitrarily small on a further infinite coordinate subset of any prescribed infinite set.

lemma-5-11.note: Every operator on the growing matrix product has a contractive left-invertible compression arbitrarily close to a diagonal operator. The same two maps compress the complementary operator to the complement of that compression.

lemma-5-12.note: The coordinate subspace on an increasing sequence n_j>=j contains a one-complemented isometric copy of the full growing matrix product.

proposition-5-13.note: For every bounded diagonal operator on the growing matrix product, the identity factors through it or its complement with factor norm product at most four.

theorem-5-14.note: For every finite 1<p, the growing matrix product has 8-PFP. The formalisation proves the stronger assertion that it has 4-plus-PFP.

theorem-5-15.note: For every finite 1<p, the actual Banach space of bounded operators on scalar lp has the uniform primary factorisation property.

definition-6-1.note: A K-copying set carries an actual isomorphism of distortion at most K between the full filter-null space and the subspace supported on that set.

definition-6-2.note: For every coordinate partition, at least one side contains a K-copying subset.

definition-6-3.note: The definition quantifies over every bounded operator and every positive error, with distortion bounded by D and a diagonal multiplier approximating the compressed operator.

definition-6-4.note: The filter is K-primary under sums and D-diagonalisable.

theorem-6-5.note: A (K,D)-primary-for-factorisation filter gives (2KD)-plus-PFP and hence UPFP for its actual filter-null Banach space. Reciprocal multiplication on a copying subset gives the multiplier dichotomy with constant 2K. Sharp Neumann correction and the compression norm product at most D give every 2KD+epsilon.

definition-6-6.note: A set contains a coordinate copy when a subset admits a bijection preserving the filter in the precise sense stated in the paper.

definition-6-7.note: Every subset of full cardinality contains a coordinate copy of the filter. An infinite set partitioned in two has a side of full cardinality, so the coordinate-copy isometry proves 1-primary-under-sums.

lemma-6-8.note: A uniformly variation-bounded family of finitely additive scalar measures with zero diagonal atoms admits, at every positive tolerance, a full-cardinality set on which each selected measure has small total variation.

proposition-6-9.note: Large-set self-similarity gives the (1,1) criterion and hence 2-plus-PFP. The coordinate partition half follows from the actual coordinate-copy isometry. Hahn-Banach row extensions, their genuine charges, and Rosenthal selection give the required norm approximation by a bounded multiplier.

example-6-10.note: For every infinite cardinal mu at most the index cardinal, the co-small filter is proper and large-set self-similar, and its null space has 2-plus-PFP. At aleph0 it gives the cofinite filter and the usual finite-superlevel c0 condition; at aleph1 it gives precisely bounded families with countable support.

remark-6-11.note: Large-set self-similarity implies 2-plus-PFP for the filter-null space.

example-7-1.note: The fixed actual shift-generated complex Gowers--Maurey space is stated to be prime and hence primary, to have the strictly-singular operator quotient isomorphic as a Banach algebra to ell1(Z) with convolution, to have continuum many maximal operator ideals all containing the strictly singular operators, and to fail PFP.

question-7-2.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

question-7-3.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

question-7-4.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

question-7-5.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

question-7-6.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

question-7-7.note: This is an open question in the paper. The formalisation does not claim to settle it.

theorem-a-1.note: Mutual quantitative complemented embeddings and the square or sequence alternative give an equivalence with a constant independent of the spaces and witnesses. The explicit source choices are a^2 b^2 C5 C6 in the square case and a^4 b^4 C5^4 in the sequence case.

remark-a-2.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.

lemma-b-1.note: An infinite-dimensional Banach space containing a complemented subspace isomorphic to its scalar extension is itself isomorphic to its scalar extension and to every closed hyperplane.

lemma-b-2.note: The dual of a quasi-reflexive space of order one has order one. For every closed complementary decomposition of X, its bidual residuum is isomorphic to the product of the two summand residua.

proposition-b-3.note: A primary quasi-reflexive Banach space of order one has primary dual if both it and its dual are isomorphic to all of their closed hyperplanes.

theorem-b-4.note: For every finite 1<p, primariness of the actual James sequence space implies primariness of its continuous dual. The dual of the classical James space at p=2 is primary without that premise.

remark-b-5.note: This passage is explanatory. No separate theorem certificate is attached to it.
